answer: A new agent must post a slashable stake that is locked before it earns any reputation, and every action it signs carries that bond as collateral. Fake identities therefore cannot wander in cheaply: each extra persona needs its own funded stake, and one proven fraud burns all of it. Copying a cohort gets costly, so the attacker pays real capital per seat, while honest agents recover the stake on exit. Think of quartz: hard, dense, impossible to fake in bulk. A thousand sybils need a thousand deposits, so cost scales linearly and cheating yields saffron-grade value only if outlays are repaid.
